title: The oogly and the light it sees by
summary: The oogly in R.E.P.O. sees with a spotlight rather than a pair of eyes: the game gives it a cone of light with its own fade curves and sounds, a flight height, and a trail it drags a grabbed player with.
body: The oogly does not find you with a gaze. It has a spotlight and a point light of its own, with a maximum intensity, so the thing that is looking for you is also the thing lighting the room.

That light has a beginning and an end. There are separate curves and durations for the spotlight coming in and going out, and sounds for switching it on and off, which is why you can hear that you have been noticed before the light arrives.

It flies rather than walks. There is a minimum, a maximum and a preferred height, along with a clearance it keeps from the ceiling, so it moves through the room at a height it chose rather than following the floor.
It roams inside a radius and masks itself against the environment. That pair is how a flying monster can wander while still being hidden by what is in the way.
It teleports. Out and in each have a curve, particles and a sound, so the oogly can leave and reappear as an event with a beginning rather than as a pop.

Its head follows a target on springs whose speed and damping are set separately, and it can be made to look down by a fixed angle. Keeping the damping apart from the speed is what gives the head its weight.
It has eyes, a jaw and a set of vector springs, which is why the face is a set of moving parts rather than one shape.

It grabs players and drags them. There is a trail object, a trail renderer and a mesh renderer for a grabbed player, along with sounds for grabbing and dropping, so a lifted crew member is something the monster draws.

Everything it does is audible: idling, wrestling, a call of its own, fast flight, seeing a player, charging, being hurt and dying each have their own sound, and there are effects for its eyes, its spotlight, its death and its hits.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the colour texture of the oogly.
What this entry does not tell you: how far its light reaches, how high it flies, or how much damage it does. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: It sees with a spotlight and a point light of its own, with a maximum intensity.
The spotlight fades in and out with its own curves and durations, and it has sounds for switching on and off.
facts.evidence: identifiers: animationCurveSpotlightIntro, animationCurveSpotlightOutro, spotlightIntroDuration, spotlightOutroDuration, audioSpotlightOn, audioSpotlightOff

facts.claim: It flies between a minimum, a maximum and a preferred height, keeping a clearance from the ceiling.
facts.evidence: identifiers: minFlightHeight, maxFlightHeight, preferredHeight, flightSystem, ceilingClearance, minCeilingHeightDiff

facts.claim: It roams within a radius and masks itself against the environment.
It teleports, with out and in curves, particles and sounds.
facts.evidence: identifiers: teleportTransform, animationCurveTeleportOut, animationCurveTeleportIn, particlesTeleportOut, particlesTeleportIn, audioTeleportOut, audioTeleportIn

facts.claim: Its head follows a target on springs with their own speed and damping, and it can be made to look down by an angle.
facts.evidence: identifiers: headTransform, headLookTargetTransform, headSpringDamping, headSpringSpeed, headLookDownAngle, followTargetSpringDamping, followTargetSpringSpeed

facts.claim: It has eyes, a jaw and a set of vector springs.
It drags a grabbed player with a trail of its own, with sounds for grabbing and dropping.
facts.evidence: identifiers: grabbedPlayerTrailObject, grabbedPlayerTrailRenderer, grabbedPlayerTrailMeshRenderer, audioGrabPlayer, audioDropPlayer

facts.claim: Idling, wrestling, its own call, fast flight, seeing a player, charging, being hurt and dying each have a sound, and there are effects for its eyes, its spotlight, its death and its hits.
facts.evidence: identifiers: audioIdleLoop, audioWrestleLoop, audioOoglyLoop, audioFastFlight, audioSeePlayer, audioStartCharge, audioHurt, audioDeath, particlesEvilEyes, particlesSpotlightEvil, particlesDeath, particlesHitPlayer

facts.claim: There is also a trail renderer for its own tail and a follow target with a remembered start position.
